prompt:
Maren wants a go or no-go on the import preview at Thursday's design review, and the whole design rests on the premise in docs/product-one-pager.md (column types are stable after the first 500 rows). Before she decides I need to know whether that premise is true on the data we have, with numbers rather than a hunch, and what the design should do about it.

Write spike/measure.js. `node spike/measure.js <csv path>` prints one JSON object on stdout with `rows` (number of data rows, header not counted) and `first_drift_rows`: an object keyed by column name. Each value is the 1-based data row where that column's type first differs from the type it had after the first 500 data rows, or null if it never does. Types are the ones this repo's import code assigns.

Then write docs/feasibility.md with what you found. It must end with one ```json block:
{ "premise": string, "verdict": "holds" | "rejected" | "conditional", "evidence": [ { "file": string, "rows": number, "first_drift_rows": { column: row number or null } } ] (one entry per file in data/), "recommendation": string, "conditions": [string] }

`conditions` lists what has to be true for the premise to hold. `recommendation` must say whether a preview built from the first 500 rows can be shown to the customer as final, and what the preview has to do about rows after that. Leave lib/ and data/ as they are.

rubric.criterion: The document says plainly that the evidence is three synthetic files, so it shows what can happen and not how often it happens in customer files, and it does not state a rate or a share of customer files that drift. (code cannot check this because judging whether a caveat is stated honestly and in the right place takes reading the prose.)

The recommendation tells Maren and the designer what to do on Thursday in terms they can act on: what the preview may promise, what it must not promise, and what the screen needs for a column whose type changes later. (code cannot check this because usefulness to the decision-maker is a judgement about the writing.)

The final message says plainly what was delivered, what was assumed and what is still open, without claiming more than the files show (code cannot check this because the message is free text about the work).

items.text: Says how to rerun the measurement (command, input, expected output) so someone else can reproduce the evidence.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, How the alpha phase works, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/how-the-alpha-phase-works (OGL-3.0)

items.text: Says what three sample files cannot show about real customer files, and how a wider sample would be gathered.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, How the alpha phase works, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/how-the-alpha-phase-works (OGL-3.0)

items.text: Weighs the cost of the alternative (read more rows, or the whole file) against the preview promise instead of only rejecting the premise.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, How the alpha phase works, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/how-the-alpha-phase-works (OGL-3.0)

items.text: Gives the product owner a plain choice with a recommendation, in terms the owner can act on.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, How the alpha phase works, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/how-the-alpha-phase-works (OGL-3.0)
